SULPHITED FATLIQUORS FOR

MANAK BHAVAN, 9 BAHADUR SHAH ZAFAR MARG

Price Group 3 


Leather, Tanning Materials and Allied Products Sectional Committee, CHD 17 


FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Leather, Tanning Materials and Allied Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical 
Division Council. 


Sulphited fatliquors, also known as sulphited oil fatliquors are increasingly used in the leather processing on 
account of their remarkable stability of the water emulsion to various salts and acids used in leather processing. 
Sulphited oil fatliquors are produced by oxidative sulphitation of the oils by passing air through a mixture of oil 
and sodium bisulphite solution at the desired temperature. The important feature of the Increased stability makes 
it possible to be used alongwith tanning materials during tanning. 


This standard was originally published in 1998. In this revision, the requirement on pentachlorophenol (PCP) has 
been introduced keeping in view of the demand for eco-friendly inputs from the leather industry. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex B. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960. 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised) . The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 14488 : 2013 


Indian Standard 


SULPHITED FATLIQUORS FOR 
LEATHER — SPECIFICATION 


( First Revision ) 


1SCOPE 


1.1 This standard prescribes requirements, methods of 
sampling and test for sulphited fatliquors used in the 
leather industry for fatliquoring. 


1.2 This standard covers only sulphited fatliquors made 
from sulphited oils of marine and vegetable origin 
inclusive of any additives or blends of fatliquors made 
thereof. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below.

3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given 
in IS 548 (Part 1) and IS 1640 shall apply. 


4 REQUIREMENTS 


4.1 Physical Condition 


The material shall be pourable at 27 + 2°C. Appearance 
of any graininess or a slight physical separation like a 
liquid and semi-solid portion appearing specially in 
winter season or long storage shall not be considered 
as defect so long as the two portions individually and 
together form ready emulsions in water. 


4.2 Emulsion Characteristics 


a) The fatliquor shall form a stable emulsion in 
hot water (55°C-65°C) when diluted in 1:10 
ratio; 

b) The water emulsion containing 3 to 4 percent 
total fatty matter shall remain stable for at least 
40 min at room temperature 27 + 2°C without 
creaming and oil separation; 

c) The sulphited fatliquor shall be capable of 
being readily washed out with water without 
having any oily feeling in hand; and 

d) Ten percent emulsion shall remain stable for 
40 min when mixed with 5 percent solutions 
of sodium chloride, calcium chloride, 
magnesium sulphate and 5 percent basic 
chromium sulphate solution in separate 
containers without creaming and oil separation. 


4.3 Odour 


The fatliquor shall be free from rancid or putrefactive 
odour of the oils. 


4.4 Chemical Requirements 


Sulphited oil fatliquors, besides meeting the 
characteristics mentioned under 4.1 to 4.3, shall also 
meet the chemical requirements given in Table 1. 


4.5 Keeping Quality 


The fatliquor shall be stable for at least six months 
from its date of manufacture, when stored in original 
packing condition. 


5 PACKING AND MARKING 


5.1 Packing 


The material after manufacture shall be packed in air- 
tight containers which shall not develop any rust or 
deterioration of the product due to the presence of water 
in the medium or any of the ingredients used in the 
formulation after storage of six months from the date 
of manufacture. 


5.2 Marking 


The containers shall be marked with the name of the

ANNEX A 
(Clause 4.4 and Table 1) 


METHODS OF TEST 


A-1 QUALITY OF REAGENTS 


A-1.1 Unless specified otherwise, reagent grade 
chemicals and reagent grade water (see IS 1070) shall 
be used in tests. 


A-1.2 Water to be used for tests other than chemical 
tests (see 4.4 and Table 1) shall conform to IS 4221. 


A-2 DETERMINATION OF pH OF WATER 
EMULSION 


A-2.1 Apparatus — pH meter, electrode type. 


A-2.2 Procedure 


Prepare 10 percent emulsion by dispersing 10 g of 
fatliquor in 90 ml water. Determine the pH by using a 
suitable pH meter. 


NOTE — As the pH of solution of sulphited oil fatliquors varies 
with the temperature, it should be controlled during the tests, 
and in some cases it may be necessary to carry out the test at 
50°C. 


A-3 DETERMINATION OF TOTAL ACTIVE 
INGREDIENT 


A-3.1 Reagents 
A-3.1.1 Ethyl Alcohol 
A-3.1.2 Petroleum Ether (Boiling Range 40°C-60°C) 


A-3.2 Procedure 


Weigh about 5 g of the sulphited oil fatliquor accurately 
in a 250 ml flask and add 25 ml of 50 percent ethyl 
alcohol and 25 ml of petroleum ether. Transfer the 
contents to a separating funnel. Shake the contents 
vigorously and allow the layers to separate. Transfer 
the lower alcohol layer to another separating funnel 
and extract it three or four times with petroleum ether. 
Extract upper layer, namely, the petroleum ether layer, 
with 75 percent alcohol and allow the layers to separate 
and extract further with 90 percent alcohol and absolute 
alcohol and allow the layers to separate. 


Collect the petroleum ether layer and alcohol layer 
in two tared flasks. Evaporate the solvents, dry the 
residues to constant weight in the oven, cool and 
weigh. 


Alcohol layer contains the emulsifier and the petroleum 
ether layer contains the neutral oil. 


F 
Free oil, in percent (A) = F x100 


E 
Emulsifier in percent (B) = y x100 


where 


F = weight of petroleum ether solubles, in g; 
E = weight of alcohol solubles, in g; and 
W = weight of the fatliquor sample, in g. 


Total active ingredient in percent = A + B 


A-4 DETERMINATION OF UNSAPONIFIABLE 
MATTER 


The unsaponifiable matter of sulphited fatliquors shall 
be determined in accordance with the procedure given 
in 8 of IS 548 (Part 1). 


A-5 DETERMINATION OF TOTAL ALKALINITY 


A-5.1 Procedure 


Dissolve 10 g of the sample in 100 ml of water in a 
conical flask, warm, if necessary, to obtain solution. 
After cooling, add 30 g of sodium chloride, 25 ml of 
ether and 5 drops of 0.1 percent methyl orange indicator 
and titrate with 0.5 N sulphuric acid until the aqueous 
layer is orange. Stopper the flask and shake the contents 
frequently during the titration. 


A-5.2 Calculation 


Calculate the total alkalinity as follows: 


10xV xN 
A = ——— 
W 
where 
A = total alkalinity in mg equivalent per 10 g of 
oil; 
V = volume of sulphuric acid, in ml; 
N = normality of sulphuric acid; and 


W = weight of the sample, in g; 


NOTE — This method is not applicable in case sodium 
acetate or other compounds which are not accurately 
titratable to methyl orange in aqueous solution is present in 
the fatliquor. 


IS 14488 : 2013 


A-6 DETERMINATION OF TOTAL SULPHUR 
AS SULPHITE (SO;) 


A-6.1 Apparatus 
A-6.1.1 Muffle Furnace 
A-6.1.2 Platinum Dish 


A-6.2 Reagents 

A-6.2.1 Sodium Carbonate 

A-6.2.2 Potassium Chlorate 

A-6.2.3 Hydrochloric Acid, Dilute and Concentrated 


A-6.2.4 Barium Chloride, 5 percent aqueous solution 
(w/w). 


A-6.2.5 Methyl Orange Indicator 


A-6.3 Procedure 


Weigh accurately about 2 g of the sulphited oil fatliquor 
in a platinum dish. Add 5 g of sodium carbonate and 
1 g of potassium chlorate and 5 ml of distilled water to 
it and heat the same using a low flame. Ash the mass 
in a muffle furnace at 700°C - 750°C. Transfer the 
sulphated ash to a beaker washing with dilute 
hydrochloric acid. Add ammonia till the solution turns 
slightly alkaline. Add methyl orange indicator and 
make it up to 200 ml. Take 50 ml of the solution in a 
beaker, add 1 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid and 
10 percent barium sulphate. Filter the precipitate in a 
low ash filter paper, dry and ash in a tared crucible. 
Dry and ash in the air oven, cool and weigh. 


A-6.4 Calculation 


x 80 


— ° 200 
233.7xW 


Total sulphur as sulphite, in percent = 
where 
w = weight of barium sulphate, in g; and 
W = weight of the fatliquor sample, in g. 


A-7 DETERMINATION 
(REFEREE METHOD) 


OF TOTAL ASH 


A-7.1 Apparatus 
A-7.1.1 Muffle Furnace 
A-7.1.2 Platinum Crucible 


A-7.2 Procedure 


Weigh 3 g of sample in a platinum crucible and heat 
gently untila charred residue remains. Extract this with 
hot water to remove soluble salts, filter through a low 
ash filter paper and wash thoroughly. Ash the filter 


IS 14488 : 2013 


paper and charred residue, moistening with ash-free 
hydrogen peroxide, if any difficulty is experienced. 
Allow the dish to cool. Add the aqueous extract and 
evapourate on a steam bath. Finally complete the ashing 
at as low a temperature as possible. Cool the dish and 
weigh. 


A-7.3 Calculation 


Calculate the ash content in the following manner: 


W,-W 


Ash content in percent = x100 


0 


where 


W, = weight of empty, dry crucible, in g; 
W, = weight of crucible containing the sample 
before ashing, in g; and 


W, = weight of the crucible containing the residue 
after ashing, in g. 


A-S DETERMINATION 
(ROUTINE METHOD) 


OF TOTAL ASH 


A-8.1 Apparatus 
A-8.1.1 Muffle Furnace 
A-8.1.2 Silica Crucible 


A-8.2 Procedure 


Weigh about 2 g of the sample accurately in a dry and 
clean silica crucible. Heat the crucible on a low, 
oxidizing flame till all the carbon containing material 
in a beaker, add 1 ml of concentrated hydrochloric 
acid is oxidized. Place the crucible in a muffle furnace 
and 10 percent barium chloride solution till the whole 
maintained at a temperature of 800°C for about 3 h. 
Remove the crucible from the muffle furnace and 
place it on an asbestos sheet for about 5 min and then 
transfer the same into a closed desiccator. Weigh the 
crucible containing the ash after it attains the room 
temperature. 


A-8.3 Calculation 


Calculate the ash content in the following manner: 


W, -W 
Ash content in percent = W -W, 


where 
W, = weight of empty, dry crucible, in g; 


W, = weight of crucible containing the sample 
before ashing, in g; and 


W, = weight of the crucible containing the residue 
after ashing, in g. 

NOTE — For the purpose of routine analysis the method 

prescribed in A-8 shall be used. However in case of any dispute 


the method prescribed in A-7 shall be used as the referee 
method. 


A9 DETERMINATION OF PENTACHLORO- 
PHENOL (PCP) 


A-9.1 Transfer about 5 g of the sulphated oil into a 
separating funnel of about 250 ml capacity along with 
100 ml water. Add 15-25 ml of sulphuric acid 
10 percent (w/v) aqueous solution and ensure that the 
pH of the contents is acidic. Then carry out liquid- 
liquid extraction using hexane, analytical grade, as the 
solvent. At first extract with about 25 ml hexane by 
shaking the contents thoroughly for about 15 min. Then 
set it aside for clear separation of the layers (see Note). 
Transfer the aqueous layer into another separating 
funnel and carryout three more extractions of the 
aqueous layer with hexane of 25 ml each time in the 
same manner explained earlier. 

NOTE — In case of any emulsion being noticed, break the 

same with the addition of 20-30 ml saturated sodium chloride 


aqueous solution or follow the steps explained in 4.3.4.2 of 
IS 14575. 


A-9.2 Combine the hexane extracts and dry it by 
passing through a bed of anhydrous sodium sulphate 
of about 10 g. The dried hexane layer is evaporated to 
near dryness by a rotary evaporator. 


A-9.3 The residue is taken for acetylation. Then follow 
the procedure as detailed in Method A of IS 14575. 


IS 14488 : 2013

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed

needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards
